title: Climacteric and non-climacteric produce — ethylene behaviour
text: Bananas, avocados and tomatoes are climacteric fruits: as they ripen they show a strong peak in respiration with high internal ethylene production, and they respond to exogenous ethylene, which speeds softening and ripening. Strawberries are non-climacteric: respiration stays roughly constant or declines until senescence, with little or no increase in internal ethylene production.
context: This chunk discusses the classification of climacteric and non-climacteric fruits based on respiration and ethylene production, sourced from the 2023 USDA AMS National Organic Program Ethylene Report.

title: How humidity speeds spoilage in the simulation
text: ShelfSense models ambient stress as an environment factor beta_env = 1 + 0.5 × clamp((RH − 50) / 50, 0, 1), so relative humidity above 50 % ages exposed products up to 1.5× faster.
context: This chunk explains the ShelfSense model's formula for calculating ambient stress and product aging based on relative humidity.

title: How humidity speeds spoilage in the simulation
text: Each product's weather_exposure (0–1) scales how much of that stress reaches it: berries, bananas, avocados and tomatoes are fully exposed; spinach 0.8, bread 0.6, chilled salmon and milk 0.2.
context: This chunk specifies the weather exposure scaling factors for different products in the ShelfSense ambient stress model.

title: How humidity speeds spoilage in the simulation
